focus: Is a re-render in plainer words still the right lane? Render-lane limits, protected-span order admissibility, and the keep/extend/split verdict

label: The render lane has four modes, all presentation-only, and its input contract carries no message text, so reordering is unrepresentable rather than disallowed

The render layer re-verifies byte identity between the displayed text and the validated text; that is self-consistency, not order preservation, and an accepted projection reports the single constant projection-accepted
The contract's only order-specific guarantee is the protected-span token sequence, compared position by position, rejected by name as PLACEHOLDER_REORDERED and fail-closed to the exact original
A prose reorder that never moves a spanned segment passes the whole current contract indistinguishably from a copy edit; the engine cannot tell the two operations apart
No order or wording observation survives into either decision record, so a detected prose reorder would not be reported as one
Verdict: keep the copy-editing lane and split cut-and-reorder into a separate declared operation; do not relax the token-order check
A spanned segment may not change position: any deviation of the token sequence from the span order is a hard rejection, not a quality downgrade
The render layer may only select between the validated projection and the exact original, and may never compose or reorder text
One lane is enough for both copy editing and cut-and-reorder
Copy editing and cut-and-reorder carry incompatible guarantees
